results.title: Accuracy of ICD-9-CM codes for identifying cardiovascular and stroke risk factors.

metadata_json.title: Clinical epidemiology of heart failure.

results.text: The aim of this paper is to review the clinical epidemiology of heart failure. The last paper comprehensively addressing the epidemiology of heart failure in Heart appeared in 2000. Despite an increase in manuscripts describing epidemiological aspects of heart failure since the 1990s, additional information is still needed, as indicated by various editorials.
results.title: Clinical epidemiology of heart failure.

metadata_json.title: 3D Chromosome Regulatory Landscape of Human Pluripotent Cells.

results.text: In this study, we describe the 3D chromosome regulatory landscape of human naive and primed embryonic stem cells. metadata_json.title: CTCF binding at the H19 imprinting control region mediates maternally inherited higher-order chromatin conformation to restrict enhancer access to Igf2.

results.title: CTCF binding at the H19 imprinting control region mediates maternally inherited higher-order chromatin conformation to restrict enhancer access to Igf2.

results.title: Specific sites in the C terminus of CTCF interact with the SA2 subunit of the cohesin complex and are required for cohesin-dependent insulation activity.

metadata_json.title: Driver mutations in histone H3.3 and chromatin remodelling genes in paediatric glioblastoma

results.text: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a lethal brain tumour in adults and children. However, DNA copy number and gene expression signatures indicate differences between adult and paediatric cases. To explore the genetic events underlying this distinction, we sequenced the exomes of 48 paediatric GBM samples. Somatic mutations in the H3.3-ATRX-DAXX chromatin remodelling pathway were identified in 44% of tumours (21/48). Recurrent mutations in H3F3A, which encodes the replication-independent histone 3 ...
results.title: Driver mutations in histone H3.3 and chromatin remodelling genes in paediatric glioblastoma

metadata_json.title: Detecting and targeting tumor relapse by its resistance to innate effectors at early recurrence

results.text: Tumor recurrence represents a major clinical challenge. Our data show that emergent recurrent tumors acquire a phenotype radically different from that of their originating primary tumors. This phenotype allows them to evade a host-derived innate immune response elicited by the progression from minimal residual disease (MRD) to actively growing recurrence. results.title: Detecting and targeting tumor relapse by its resistance to innate effectors at early recurrence
